page_title: Mining Twitter Data with Python (Part 1: Collecting data)

summary.title: Mining Twitter Data with Python (Part 1: Collecting data)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to register a Twitter app, authenticate with Tweepy, and collect tweets, user lists and live streams as JSON using Python.
takeaways: Register an app at apps.twitter.com to get consumer key, consumer secret, access token and access secret.
Use Tweepy's OAuthHandler and tweepy.API to authenticate and access Twitter's REST API.
Use tweepy.Cursor to iterate over timelines, followers and friends, and store each object's _json dictionary.
Use the Streaming API with a StreamListener subclass and filter(track=[...]) to collect live tweets, saved one per line.
Respect Twitter's rate limits and terms when collecting or distributing datasets.
summary.summary: The article is the first part of a series on mining Twitter data with Python. It explains how to register a Twitter application and obtain OAuth credentials, then installs and configures the Tweepy library (version 3.3.0 at the time, with notes about later releases). It demonstrates reading the home timeline, followers and user tweets through Tweepy's Cursor, and storing raw JSON from each status. It finishes with a streaming example that writes tweets matching #python to a file, and it notes rate limits and data-sharing restrictions.
